title: AIDA observed record
description: What a model saw when it looked at one work order's surfaces through a browser, at <task folder>/implementation/observed-<order id>.json, for an order whose proof is observe (live-run row 104). The orchestrator writes it after the implementer returns: it opens each surface the order names, at each viewport the surface file declares, judges each of the order's done-when rows against what renders, and saves each screenshot under implementation/observed-<order id>/<surface>-<viewport>.png. `build-record --observed <path>` reads it as the order's own check, `observed`, met when every row is met. It refuses a file that does not match this shape (exit 93), a row whose screenshot is not on disk (94), a surface the order does not name (95) and a doneWhen the order does not hold (96). The judge is always a model: a person accepts or rejects the observation at completion, and that answer lives in the completion record, never here.

order.description: The work order's own id. build-record refuses a record naming another order.

observedAt.description: The UTC date the model looked, YYYY-MM-DD.

judgedBy.description: One value. A model looked, and the record says so: the live run filed this look as a person's checklist, which put the wrong actor on the record. `close` copies this judge onto the criteria the order owns, so rowsJudgedByModel counts them and a person returning can list them.

rows.description: One row per done-when sentence per surface per viewport. Every done-when row of the order is judged at every surface and viewport the order reaches; a row missing here is a look nobody took, and the check is met only when every row present is met.

doneWhen.description: One of the order's own done-when rows, verbatim. The sentence the model judged.

surface.description: A surface id the order names, as the surface file registers it.

viewport.description: A viewport name from the surface file's viewports list.

screenshot.description: The image the judgement was made from, an absolute path under implementation/observed-<order id>/. build-record refuses a row whose image is not on disk.

verdict.description: Whether the page showed what the sentence says. The two words every check in this stage uses for a look that was taken.

note.description: What the model saw, in one or two sentences, so a person reading the completion question knows what was judged without opening the image.
